project: WO-D1 — Document Packaged Factories with Worked Examples
description: Replace the flat packaged-Factory overview with canonical operator-ready reference documentation for all fifteen current first-party @you/* Factories. Each entry will explain purpose, live invocation signature, accepted worker roles and provider/model overrides, prerequisites or side effects, expected primary output shape, and one copy-ready example verified exactly as shown against the current you binary, with special emphasis on making @you/subagent usable without production trial and error.

context.customerAsk: Deliver WO-D1 documentation in canonical docs/reference/ Markdown with a description and one worked example for every packaged Factory, including what @you/subagent is for, each Factory's invocation signature, accepted workers/providers, and expected output shape. Execute every CLI invocation shown in the new documentation against the current binary and paste or behaviorally assert real output. Keep the binding cut list from docs/temp/work-order.md, run make docs-reference-smoke and make verify-fast, and deliver through actual PR merge.
context.problem: The packaged-Factory reference is primarily a name table plus representative commands. It does not give each Factory an independently usable worked example or consistently describe role-specific worker/provider inputs and returned output. Operators consequently discovered @you/subagent invocation semantics by trial and error during production, while other examples can be copied without enough information to predict accepted flags, prerequisites, side effects, or output.
context.solution: Expand the canonical packaged-Factory reference into a consistent operator guide. Give every current packaged Factory a focused entry containing purpose, suitable use, exact live invocation signature, worker roles and supported provider/model override behavior, prerequisites or material side effects, expected output shape, and one copy-ready worked example with real current-binary output evidence. Organize related entries for scanning, retain root docs only as routing material, and avoid engine, provider, storage, UI, API, and generated-contract changes.

acceptanceCriteria: The canonical docs/reference/ packaged-Factory topic gives each of the fifteen current first-party @you/* Factories an independently understandable description, suitable-use guidance, invocation signature, accepted worker roles and provider/model override behavior, prerequisites or material side effects, and expected output shape.

Every packaged Factory has one copy-ready worked CLI example, and every CLI invocation added or changed in the topic is executed exactly as shown against the current you binary during implementation; corresponding real output is pasted in the documentation or captured by a direct behavioral assertion, with reviewer-visible evidence and no invented flags or output.

The @you/subagent entry explicitly explains its bounded read-only purpose, request binding, optional provider/model/reasoning inputs supported by the live signature, single worker role, and primary-result output behavior, and its worked example succeeds as documented.

Documentation distinguishes orchestration behavior, required environment/model prerequisites, potentially long-running or workspace-changing behavior, and machine-readable versus human-readable output where those facts affect safe operator use, without promising unsupported providers, flags, determinism, or exact model prose.

Scope remains limited to WO-D1 canonical reference documentation and direct documentation behavior evidence: root docs remain routing material, and there is no local-model execution harness, llama-server trace testing, Gemma validation, new ACP lane, wrapper-layer multimodal transformation, storage engine work, public API change, generated contract change, or broad unrelated cleanup.

Quality gates pass: make docs-reference-smoke, make verify-fast, applicable typecheck and focused tests, and no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file reconciliation are resolved, and the PR is actually merged; an opened, green, approved, or ready-to-merge PR is not complete.

userStories.title: Establish the operator-facing entry contract and discovery guidance
userStories.description: As an operator, I want a consistent structure and trustworthy discovery guidance so I can compare packaged Factories and understand how live signatures, defaults, outputs, and examples should be read.
acceptanceCriteria: The topic explains how packaged Factories are discovered and materialized, how to inspect a Factory's current live invocation help, and how omitted role provider/model values use operator defaults, using commands verified against the current binary.

A consistent entry contract is used for every Factory: purpose and suitable use, invocation signature, accepted worker roles and provider/model overrides, prerequisites or side effects, expected output shape, one worked invocation, and real output evidence.
The topic explains that model-generated prose is not byte-stable and describes output shape without presenting one model response as a deterministic guarantee.
Navigation supports finding an individual Factory without turning root documentation into a duplicate guide.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass, including make docs-reference-smoke
userStories.notes: Established the canonical packaged-factories operator guide with discovery/materialization guidance, a shared seven-part entry contract, family-based catalog navigation, provider/model default behavior, and non-byte-stable model-output guidance. Registered the existing topic as `you docs packaged-factories`, updated the packaged docs indexes and user-visible smoke coverage, and captured live `you factory list`, `you run --named @you/goal --help`, and `you docs packaged-factories` evidence from a freshly built current-source binary. `make docs-reference-smoke`, `make verify-fast`, `make readme-check`, and `git diff --check` pass. The broad `make lint` tier reached the existing 176-violation `pkg-boundary` baseline after all changed-file-relevant lint checks passed; no changed file is among those baseline violations. Detailed per-Factory entries remain scoped to stories 002-006.

userStories.title: Document @you/subagent as a bounded read-only call
